newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico completes refinancing with latest Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico completes refinancing with latest Eurobond.

text.p: The placement of Mexico's latest bond issue, a 750 million mark 11-year Eurobond, completes the $6 billion debt restructuring package it outlined last month, a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"There was a lot of demand in the market for our instruments, so we took the opportunity to complete the restructuring package," the senior official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
Mexico announced in mid-June it would call $6.0 billion in five-year floating rate notes issued in mid-1996.

That floating rate note had helped Mexico pay back part of what it owed to the U.S. government for emergency aid received after the 1994-1995 peso crash. The notes received an investment grade rating, since they were backed by oil revenues, but the use of the revenues to guarantee the bonds also touched a sensitive political point in Mexico.
The Finance Ministry plans to finance the August 6 amortization of the floating rate notes with debt launched earlier this year and with its latest issues.
Among the moves planned by the United Mexican States (UMS), the formal name of the federal government, was to expand its 10-year global bond issued in January to $1.5 billion from $1.0 billion.
The UMS also issued a seven-year 500 billion lira bond recently. The 750 million mark issue is the latest and last of the restructuring.
"With this issue we complete the package. It sends a very important signal," the government official said.
The mark issue has a coupon of 8.0 percent and a spread of 252 basis points over similar U.S. Treasuries.
It was placed mainly with institutional investors in Europe, principally in Germany, Luxembourg and Switzerland.
Mexico last placed a mark bond in February, issuing a 12-year 1.5 billion mark bond at 264 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
In September 1996 it placed a 1.5 billion marks eight-year issue at 304 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Over the last two years, the UMS has issued mark bonds at terms of five, seven, eight, 11, and 12 years.
